title: Finishing a typed title and picking a dissolve land inside 50 ms
goal: Command Return on a typed title over a video and a click on the Cross dissolve tile at a cut now hold the app for about 55 to 65 ms and 47 to 53 ms, down from 200 ms and 80 ms. Getting both under the 50 ms the video goals promise takes the last frame of lag out of finishing a title and picking a transition.
notes: Carried from finishing-a-typed-title-on-a-video-never-stalls (2026-10-16), whose log has the traces. Numbers at its commit, markers down, three runs: after Command Return 64.2 / 64.6 / 54.5 ms (worst pass is either the commit's own pass, 55-62 ms, or an effect pane arriving ~0.5 s later, up to 80 ms once); tile 53.2 / 49.9 / 47.2 ms. Attribution (xctrace Time Profiler, attach to the probe, export time-profile, cut to the pass): commit pass = ~10 ms harness/window performKeyEquivalent walk + ~45 ms diffuse SwiftUI graph update (timeline gains a Title track, canvas, menu commands body, panel) + ~8 ms AX. Moving the hand-back to Select a turn later was tried and did NOT help (61.8 ms; the landing is the cost, not the pick). Effect panes: each shadow pane is ~8 rows built in one pass plus SwiftUI's AccessibilityNode.updateFocus walk over every focusable view in the window (20-80 ms, half of it swift_conformsToProtocol for new view types on first use); splitting a pane's rows across passes is the next lever. Tile pass: diffuse graph update after setTransition (document change, pickCut, playhead to the cut, picker closing); the transition form already arrives a pass later. | 2026-10-18 DONE. What landed: (1) EditorState.catchUpOnTheNextPass + readingALatePass/buildingALatePass (LookRowsReading.swift): for the pass of a marked edit, look rows (panel sections) and late-pass reads (TimelineTrackRow, its lane, ClipPiecesBar, CaptionCuesLayer, CaptionWordsLane, TimelineDock grid, InspectorPanel's section list) are told about the document a pass later; LateTrackRows holds the timeline's track list unchanged in that pass. Marked edits: new text block on a video (EditorState+Text) and the transition picker's tile (TransitionPicker). For every other edit the late-pass revision moves synchronously, so nothing else changes. (2) Menu bar reads document/history unwatched and watches menuDocumentRevision, bumped a pass later (EditorState+MenuPlayhead, Next's pro menu bar only). (3) setTransition(picksLater:) picks the cut + moves the playhead a pass later for the picker tile. (4) Effects list pieces: settings a pass after the effect's header rows, a shadow's Distance/Direction/Opacity a pass after those, effects spaced 3 passes apart. GOTCHAS: DispatchQueue.main.async does NOT reach the next pass (the run loop services the main queue before it sleeps); use NextRunLoopPass. Every earlier 'X a pass later, no gain' experiment (pick later, close picker later) was this bug. A marked edit makes several history changes (setTransition then the pick's selection flush), so the flag has to hold for the whole pass, not one change. Closing the picker alone costs ~38 ms of the ~50: a whole-window SwiftUI update floor, not any one view.
acceptance: In an-editing-session-walk, the wait after Command Return on the typed title shows no single main thread pass over 50 ms, in three runs in a row
Picking Cross dissolve from the At this cut tiles holds under 50 ms in three runs in a row
The walk's two timing claims (today 100 ms and 65 ms) are tightened to 50 ms
